title: Adaptive refund queue and grace-crediting for metering ingestion latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers and support threads call out invoices with overage line items caused by delayed usage ingestion (connector latency, delayed logs, or security-questionnaire holds). Current manual refund and credit processes are slow and error-prone. This ticket scopes an end-to-end operational model: provisional credits (grace credits) issued automatically into an escrow/refund queue, an automatic reconciliation pipeline that clears or finalizes credits after ingestion finishes, and a human review path for disputed or ambiguous cases. The goal is to reduce mean time to remediate billing disputes, prevent application outages tied to sudden overage enforcement, and produce audit-grade ledger entries required by Finance and compliance.
acceptance_criteria: System issues provisional credit within 24 hours of detecting a downstream ingestion gap of >= 6 hours for enterprise orgs with active SSO/security questionnaire holds
Provisional credits are represented in billing UI as 'Pending Credit' with clear reason, amount, and expected reconciliation date
Automated reconciliation job runs daily and either finalizes credit (post-reconciliation) or creates a high-confidence candidate for manual review with a summary of evidence
All provisional credits and final adjustments produce immutable ledger entries and an audit trail accessible to Finance and customer success
Customers receive event notifications (email + console bell) when provisional credit is applied and when finalized, and can open a billing dispute which pauses finalization
End-to-end tests and load tests demonstrate the reconciliation pipeline scales to median enterprise volume (10k *events/day) without causing >3s tail latency on billing-reads
proposal: We will implement a two-layer approach: (1) a short-lived provisional credit mechanism that can be programmatically issued when metering irregularities are detected, and (2) a reconciliation pipeline that ingests late usage, re-evaluates the original provisional credit, and either finalizes it as a refund/offset or marks it for manual review. Provisional credits will live in an 'escrow' balance namespace separate from earned credits to avoid impacting revenue recognition until finalization. The reconciliation pipeline will implement deterministic heuristics (time window, token-level match rate, customer-specific connector health signals) to auto-finalize with high confidence, and push low-confidence cases to a new 'billing-review' queue surfaced in the Console for CS/Finance.
decisions: Escrow approach accepted over immediate ledger reversal to preserve auditability
Default quarantine window set to 14 days for enterprise customers; configurable per-contract (min 7 days, max 30 days)
Auto-finalization threshold: >=95% match on late-usage attribution OR delta < $50 -> auto-finalize; otherwise enqueue for manual review
Notifications: customers and account owners will be notified at apply/finalize steps; legal/finance will receive a weekly digest of finalized/manual credits
We will not alter existing invoices after finalization; instead, we will issue credit memos to keep invoice immutability

E2E tests and load testing in staging, including reseller/org edge cases (QA)
Customer communications: templated emails and CS playbook for outreach (CS/PM)
Security/legal review for escrow accounting and customer-facing messaging (LEGAL)

Schedule pilot with 3 enterprise customers for early validation (PM/CS)
